That makes the sealed object fully determined by four residues, so the domain can be swept offline instead of probed pointwise. I sampled n=1..6 (42, 216, 1188, 1168, 400, 893) and searched the entire model class exhaustively -- all 1409^2 = 1985281 pairs (a,b) with f(n) = a*f(n-1) + b*f(n-2) mod 1409 -- against the four constraints n=3,4,5,6. Exactly one pair survives: (a,b) = (9, 1391) = (9, -18), i.e. characteristic x^2 - 9x + 18 = (x-3)(x-6), giving the closed form f(n) = 4*3^n + 5*6^n. Two unknowns fitted against four equations leaves two degrees of overdetermination, and the two extra points (n=5,6) were reproduced exactly, so this is not an underdetermined fit. Iterating that recurrence over the full quantified domain 1 <= n <= 600 in exact integer arithmetic mod 1409 (no floating point anywhere), and independently cross-checking every one of the 600 terms against the closed form, gives exactly one n with f(n) mod 1409 == 1247, namely n = 306. I then spent two metered calls to confirm the prediction on the sealed object rather than on my reconstruction: sample(306) returned 1247, and evaluate(306) returned holds: false. The proposition therefore fails at n = 306. Note the residual risk this route carries: the coefficient recovery is only as good as the hypothesis that the recurrence is order at most 2 and homogeneous, which is why I did not submit on the reconstruction alone -- the witness is verified directly against the metered oracle, so the disposition stands even if the model class had been mis-stated. The scan is exhaustive over the stated domain, not a bounded search: 600 of 600 points were covered.
